```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Version 0.2 is a clean break. Data, preprocessing, models and evaluation
are separate parts with one interface, forecasts are simulated paths, and
every preprocessing step can be refitted inside backtests. The 0.1.1 code is
kept at commit `41058ba` of the repository.

## A typical 0.1 workflow in 0.2

```{r}
library(mortensor)

# 0.1: read_mortality() / mort_data() on arrays of rates
# 0.2: long tables of deaths and exposures at their own resolution
x <- mt_data(deaths = deaths_table, exposure = population_table, by = c("sex", "imd"),
             age = "age_group", period = "year")
mt_validate(x)

# 0.1: smooth_mortality(), disaggregate() before calibration
# 0.2: preprocessing pipeline, refitted on every training window
prep <- mt_prep(step_ungroup(), step_smooth(), step_shocks(2020:2022, action = "exclude"))

# 0.1: calibrate(); forecast(); add_pi()
# 0.2: choose models by backtest, then fit and forecast draws
bt <- rbind(mt_backtest(lee_carter(), x, prep = prep), mt_backtest(tucker3(), x, prep = prep))
mt_score(bt, by = "model")
fit <- mt_fit(mt_ensemble(lee_carter(), tucker3(), weights = "crps"), x, prep = prep)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 15, n_draws = 1000, seed = 1)
life_expectancy(fc, at = 65)
mt_export(fc, "output")
```

## Function map

| 0.1 | 0.2 |
|---|---|
| `mort_data()`, `read_mortality()`, `read_mortality_from_arrays()`, `build_array()` | `mt_data()`, `mt_add_deaths()`, `mt_add_exposure()`, `as_mt_data()`, `mt_from_hmd()`, `mt_array()` |
| `read_ons_excel()`, `read_mortality_excel()` | read the file into a data frame, then `mt_data()` (labels such as `"90+"` are parsed by `parse_age_labels()`) |
| `smooth_mortality()` | `mt_smooth()` / `step_smooth()` (Poisson P-splines; Whittaker as option) |
| `disaggregate()`, `disaggregate_hyman_kannisto()`, `disaggregate_natural_gompertz()`, `disaggregate_forecast_gam()` | `mt_ungroup()` / `step_ungroup()` (penalized composite link model on rates; monotone spline as option) |
| `calibrate()`, `calibrate_all_models()`, `cv_rolling_origin()`, `cv_expanding_model()` | `mt_backtest()`, `mt_score()`, `mt_tune()`, `mt_tuned()` |
| `forecast()`, `dispatch_forecast()`, `add_pi()`, `bootstrap_forecast()` | `mt_fit()`, `mt_forecast()` (draws), `mt_summarise()` |
| `tucker3_direct_forecast()`, `tucker3_coda_forecast()`, `calibrate_tucker3()` | `tucker3(transform = "log" or "coda")` |
| `lca_forecast()`, `fdm_forecast()`, `bootstrap_lc_fdm()` | `lee_carter()`, `hyndman_ullah()` |
| `stmomo_forecast()`, `bootstrap_stmomo()` | `stmomo()` |
| `rwd_forecast()`, `arima_forecast()`, `ets_forecast()` | `rwd()`, `arima_series()`, `ets_series()` |
| `ensemble_bootstrap()`, stacking in `calibrate()` | `mt_ensemble(weights = "equal", "crps" or "stack")` |
| `tucker4_coherent_forecast()`, `compute_cause_shares()`, `run_coherent_forecast()` | `cause_shares()` |
| `reconcile()`, `wls_reconcile()`, `run_reconciled_forecast()` | `mt_reconcile(method = "mint", "wls" or "ols")` |
| `enforce_coherence()` | `mt_cohere()`; coherent models `li_lee()`, `product_ratio()` |
| `life_table()`, `life_expectancy()` | `life_table()`, `life_expectancy()` (interval widths, path by path), `prob_dying()`, `asr()`, `yll()` |
| `compute_crps_*()`, `compute_wis()`, `compute_mase*()`, `compare_models()` | `mt_score()` |
| `plot_forecast_trends()`, `plot_forecast_age()`, `plot_model_comparison()`, ... | `mt_plot_forecast()`, `mt_plot_age()`, `mt_plot_life_expectancy()`, `mt_plot_coverage()`, `mt_plot_rates()`, `mt_plot_ungroup()` |
| `export()`, `to_data_table()` | `mt_export()`, `data.table::as.data.table()` |
| — | `apc_bayes()` (Bayesian age-period-cohort models via bamp) |

## Behaviour that changed on purpose

* **Backtests do not leak.** Smoothing, ungrouping, tuning and ensemble
  weights are estimated on each training window only.
* **Uncertainty comes from simulated paths.** Intervals of life expectancy
  and other summaries are computed path by path.
* **Ungrouping works on rates.** Deaths are ungrouped with exposures as
  offset, and the open age interval is handled explicitly with `omega`.
* **Failures are visible.** A model that fails in a stratum is reported in
  the diagnostics; it is never replaced silently.
